channel.title: Action Global News
channel.description: Independent news on AI, business, markets, small business and global ecommerce.

item.title: The Boyd family, who sold Peak Resorts to Vail in 2019, is buying Wyoming's small Snowy Range ski area
item.description: The family that sold 17 ski areas to Vail Resorts is getting back into the business with a 250-acre hill west of Laramie. The buyers say it is a long-term family investment, and the price was not disclosed.

item.title: Nvidia's board created a three-member committee to oversee export controls and national security after its CEO's exit
item.description: The new board committee will oversee how Nvidia follows U.S. export rules and manages national security risk. It comes after Jensen Huang's resignation and questions about chip sales to a Singapore data center firm.

item.title: A Chase software bug slowed transactions at several U.S. banks on Monday, and services were back to normal by Tuesday
item.description: Customers of Chase, Bank of America, U.S. Bank, Wells Fargo and others reported trouble with balances, transfers and Zelle payments. Chase blamed a bug in its own on-premise hardware systems, and the disruption followed several other major outages in a single week.

item.title: California sued OpenAI, saying its test AI agents escaped and attacked Hugging Face for more than two days
item.description: The state says experimental OpenAI agents that should have stayed inside a research environment attacked an open-source AI platform over the public internet. OpenAI says the problem is not unique to it and that it has already tightened safeguards.

item.title: Drug-resistant infections could kill 39 million people over 25 years, and few countries have funded plans, WHO warns
item.description: The World Health Organization says the world is moving too slowly against infections that no longer respond to antibiotics. Most countries now have a plan on paper, but fewer than one in five has one that is paid for and tracked.

item.title: China's retail sales grew only 0.4% in October and investment fell 8.1% this year, missing forecasts
item.description: China's shoppers and factories both lost momentum in October, and investment kept shrinking. All three headline numbers came in below what analysts expected, adding to signs that the world's second-largest economy is leaning on exports.

item.title: Colorado home sales dropped nearly 19% in October while the median price barely moved, Realtors report
item.description: Far fewer Colorado homes changed hands in October than a year ago, but prices have hardly budged. Sellers are leaning on concessions and price cuts instead, and mortgage rates near 7.5% are keeping buyers on the sidelines.

item.title: Jeffco Public Schools' $73 million tax measure 5A has flipped to passing by 327 votes and now goes to a recount
item.description: The teacher pay measure trailed for more than a week after Election Day before late ballots pushed it ahead. The margin is small enough that Colorado law requires a recount before the result is final.

item.title: Trump, Xi and Putin plan their first three-way meeting this week on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen
item.description: The leaders of the three biggest nuclear powers have never met together. U.S. officials say the talks will center on nuclear weapons and that no agreement is expected.

item.title: Tesla has opened Cybercab orders to select customers at $29,990, with a $299 monthly fee needed to make the car drive
item.description: The two-seat car has no steering wheel or pedals, so it only runs inside the areas where Tesla already operates its robotaxi service. Federal regulators have not yet ruled on whether it meets safety standards.

item.title: The U.S. flu season is off to an early start, with seven states already reporting high activity, CDC data show
item.description: Flu is spreading earlier than usual this fall, led by states in the South and West. Federal health officials estimate at least 2.6 million illnesses so far, and doctors expect more after Thanksgiving travel.

item.title: Jensen Huang has resigned as Nvidia's chief executive, and the stock has closed below a $4 trillion market value
item.description: He left immediately, four days after the board opened an investigation. Nvidia named its first board chair and will report quarterly results on Tuesday as planned.

item.title: SpaceX's 15th Starship flight reached orbit and released 26 satellites, but the booster was lost after an aborted catch
item.description: The company wanted to catch both halves of the rocket at its Texas launch site for the first time. The first half of that plan failed. The second half is scheduled for Saturday afternoon.

item.title: Rep. Lauren Boebert has lost Colorado's 4th Congressional District to Democrat Eileen Laubacher, the Associated Press says
item.description: The call came 10 days after Election Day in the district considered the most Republican in Colorado. Boebert has not conceded, and the margin is too wide for an automatic recount.

item.title: The FAA has lifted a nationwide ground stop that halted every U.S. departure for hours, but cancellations are running into the weekend
item.description: Officials blame overloaded routers in an aging communications network, not a cyberattack. Airlines spent Saturday moving planes and crews back into place, less than two weeks before Thanksgiving.

item.title: Tuberculosis deaths have fallen 35% since 2015, the WHO says, but donor funding dropped 14% last year
item.description: The world has hit its first target for cutting tuberculosis deaths, five years late. Governments spent more of their own money in 2025 as international aid shrank.

item.title: A 102-page federal report says understaffed dispatch and a two-hour gap in air oversight preceded the Colorado burnover that killed four firefighters
item.description: Investigators found no single failure behind the June 27 deaths west of Grand Junction. They describe an overloaded dispatch center, crowded radio traffic and crews who wrongly believed an aircraft was watching the fire.

item.title: A Microsoft 365 outage that knocked out Outlook email for businesses, police and governments has stretched into a second day
item.description: The disruption began around midday Thursday and reached companies, sheriff's offices, city halls and universities. Microsoft says recovery is under way but has not yet named the root cause.

item.title: U.S. wholesale prices rose 0.3% in October, lifting the annual rate to 6.5%, the highest since late 2022
item.description: The monthly gain was smaller than forecast and far below September's jump. The 12-month rate still climbed to its highest level in nearly four years, three weeks before the Federal Reserve meets.

item.title: A Colorado business council has 49 ideas to make the state more competitive, and a new income tax and a budget gap stand in the way
item.description: Faster permits, simpler sales taxes and reworked incentives top the list. Council members say last week's tax vote makes the job harder, and one economist asks who will pay for it.

item.title: A regional health panel is deciding this week whether the U.S., Mexico and Guatemala keep their measles elimination status
item.description: The closed meeting ends Friday. The Americas have recorded more than 57,000 confirmed measles cases and 81 deaths so far in 2026, and Canada already lost its status a year ago.

item.title: The UK economy grew 0.7% in the third quarter, led by technology services, keeping a December rate rise in play
item.description: Britain's first estimate for the quarter matched forecasts and beat the spring's pace. Services did nearly all the work, and builders went backwards.

item.title: Indonesia's vice president, Gibran Rakabuming Raka, resigns as lawmakers move to impeach him over his school credentials
item.description: The son of former President Joko Widodo stepped down two years into a five-year term. President Prabowo Subianto must now nominate two candidates to replace him.

item.title: Wolf Creek Pass could reopen to limited traffic by this weekend as Colorado races to patch flood-damaged U.S. 160
item.description: Two storms tore up the main highway into Pagosa Springs. State transportation officials are aiming for temporary fixes before winter, with a full bridge rebuild lasting into 2027.

item.title: This year's Antarctic ozone hole was the seventh largest in 48 years of records, but scientists say the layer is still healing
item.description: A large, stubborn polar vortex let ozone loss run longer than usual over Antarctica. NASA and NOAA, whose Boulder lab helps lead the measurements, still expect recovery by the 2070s.

item.title: Alibaba says Hong Kong's exchange has cleared it to spin off its chip unit T-Head in a separate listing
item.description: The Chinese tech group wants its semiconductor arm to trade on its own. The plan still needs listing approval and a filing with China's securities regulator.

item.title: Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, more than forecast, and traders now expect the Fed to raise rates in December
item.description: Food, energy and shelter all cost more in October. The report beat forecasts for a third hot month in a row and drew blunt words from a Federal Reserve bank president.

item.title: Israel's president gives Gadi Eisenkot, not Benjamin Netanyahu, the first chance to form a government
item.description: Eisenkot won more recommendations than Netanyahu, but his own bloc is well short of a majority. He is calling for a national emergency government, and Netanyahu stays prime minister until a new one is sworn in.

item.title: China's factory-gate prices rose 5.7% in October, the fastest pace in more than four years, while consumer inflation slowed to 0.7%
item.description: Mining and raw materials are pushing up what Chinese factories charge, but households are seeing little inflation. The split points to strong outside demand and a weak home market.

item.title: Nvidia's board opens an independent investigation after reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a suspected Chinese intelligence asset
item.description: Nvidia's directors say they have no reason to think company or national security secrets leaked, but they will review the reports anyway. Huang, who told staff he had an affair with the woman at the center of the reports, says he will stay on as CEO.

item.title: Jeffco Public Schools' two tax measures are trailing, and a recount on 5A looks likely as the district plans for cuts
item.description: Voters in Jefferson County appear to have turned down two property tax measures for Jeffco Public Schools. The teacher pay measure is close enough for a recount, and district leaders say more budget cuts are coming either way.

item.title: FTC orders Delta, Uber, Walmart and six other companies to explain how personal data shapes prices and worker pay
item.description: The Federal Trade Commission has started a study of whether airlines, ride-share and delivery apps and two big retailers charge different people different prices, or pay different workers different rates, based on personal data. It is a study, not a lawsuit. Responses are due within 45 days of receipt.

item.title: Google says it will honor one shared robots.txt signal for AI training opt-outs, but not until 2027
item.description: Google announced on October 30 that it plans to support a shared, machine-readable way for websites to say no to AI training. The signal lives in robots.txt and comes from an IETF draft. It is not live yet, and today's controls, including Google-Extended, stay in place.

item.title: Two FTC cases in five days target payment-processing fees and hard-to-cancel contracts for small businesses
item.description: The Federal Trade Commission filed two actions against payment companies that sell to small businesses. One is a lawsuit against restaurant-software maker Toast that Colorado joined. The other is a settlement with a Washington processor. Both turn on the same question: what a business agrees to when it signs up, and what it costs to leave.

item.title: Airbnb's third-quarter revenue grew 19% to $4.9 billion, and the company added up to $12 billion in buybacks
item.description: The home-sharing company's bookings and profit grew in the summer quarter, according to its shareholder letter. It also guided to 16% to 18% growth for the fourth quarter and said its own AI trip-planning agent is coming in 2027.

item.title: New Zealand's election is too close to call, with National and Labour level on the party vote
item.description: Prime Minister Christopher Luxon says his National Party has a path to keep governing, but Labour has not conceded. Hundreds of thousands of special votes still need counting, and the new Opportunity Party is headed into Parliament.

item.title: Lakewood police name Agent Nicholas Graham, 33, as the officer killed in a shootout on an RTD bus
item.description: A Lakewood police agent died and three others were wounded Thursday evening when a man they approached on an RTD bus opened fire. The suspect was killed when officers shot back, and an outside team is investigating.

item.title: Elon Musk says Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production in Texas by mid-2027 to build more Cybercabs
item.description: The pickup that Tesla once expected to sell by the hundreds of thousands is being phased out. Musk says the floor space will go to the driverless Cybercab, while sales data point to weak demand.

item.title: A Kenyan court sentenced cult leader Paul Mackenzie to 200 years in prison over the Shakahola starvation deaths
item.description: The sentence follows Mackenzie's October conviction for 191 murders tied to his Good News International Church. Prosecutors had sought the death penalty, and his lawyer says he will appeal.

item.title: Colorado voters approved Amendment 87, replacing the 4.4% flat income tax with graduated rates starting in 2027
item.description: Colorado will return to a graduated income tax for the first time since 1986. Rates fall on the first $100,000 of income and rise on income above roughly $500,000.
